questions.prompt: In which currency does the organisation report its technology spend?
questions.intent: Record the reporting currency so that revenue and spend bands, figures and the report use the client's own currency. Removes the silent assumption that every client reports in US dollars.
questions.answerDesign: Choose the currency in which the technology budget and spend are reported to leadership. This is a labelling fact: no answer is better than another and it changes no score.

options.label: Other (record the three-letter currency code in the note)

scoring.note: Sets the currency shown on CORE-03 and CORE-04 band labels, on every figure in the report, and the clientCurrency field of the saved record (amplify/data/resource.ts lines 106 and 131 already have it; no page element sets it today). Sets the wording of CTX-02. Carried to the FinOps IQ hand-off so the two tools are never added together across currencies without a registered, dated rate. No score. Never re-weights a score (GLOBAL-COVERAGE rule).
scoring.basis: LTM heuristic for the list: major trading currencies (BIS 2025 ranking, partial) plus the currencies of the markets named in coverage.ts and the owner's focus (EU, UK, Switzerland, India, Gulf, Latin America, South Africa). Option IDs are ISO 4217 codes. 'Reporting currency' follows the vocabulary of IAS 21 (presentation currency), not its accounting rules.

questions.prompt: Roughly what share of annual technology spend is invoiced or priced in a currency other than your reporting currency?
questions.intent: Record foreign-currency exposure of technology spend (cloud and SaaS invoiced by global providers, vendor contracts, offshore labour) as context for commercial and budget-risk wording.
questions.answerDesign: Include spend that a provider prices in another currency even when you are invoiced locally. A rough share is enough; Unknown is a valid answer.

scoring.note: Feeds a constraint line in the commercial section of the report: where the share is 15% or more, cost figures and savings ranges move with exchange rates and the report says so; where UNKNOWN, the report records that currency exposure is not tracked (a visibility fact, not a score). Handed to FinOps IQ, which plans a billing-versus-reporting currency question (GLOBAL-COVERAGE, FinOps F3). No score. Never re-weights a score (GLOBAL-COVERAGE rule).
scoring.basis: LTM heuristic for the bands (no published distribution of foreign-currency share of technology spend was found; none is claimed). The two currencies in the FOCUS 1.2 columns, PricingCurrency and BillingCurrency, show that cost data already treats a vendor's price currency and the invoice currency as separate facts, which is why the prompt says 'invoiced or priced'.

questions.prompt: In which regions does the organisation run technology operations or incur material technology spend?
questions.intent: Record the regions of operation so the report can state which markets it does and does not assess, and so wording and cautions fit the client's regions.
questions.answerDesign: Select every region where the organisation has material technology staff, facilities, providers or spend. Do not select a region for a few customers only.

options.label: European Union and European Economic Area
Asia-Pacific excluding India (for example Singapore, Japan, Australia, China)
Middle East (for example the Gulf states)

scoring.note: Feeds (1) the Cost IQ coverage statement (CQ5): the report names the regions the client selected and says that Cost IQ does not assess legal, tax or regulatory obligations in any of them, so local advice is needed (a client-specific version of noRegulatoryCoverage in coverage.ts). Mapping to the coverage MARKETS ids: EU to eu; UK to uk; CH to ch; NORTH_AMERICA to us and ca; INDIA to in; APAC_OTHER to sg, hk, jp, kr, cn, au, nz; MIDDLE_EAST to gcc (the Middle East is wider than the gcc entry); LATAM to latam; AFRICA to za (Africa is wider than the za entry). (2) The caveat on published figures: where a published value range comes from a global or other-region sample, the report says so for the client's regions (GLOBAL-COVERAGE, benchmark rule). (3) A routing suggestion to Sovereign IQ when EU, UK or CH is selected together with PUBLIC_CLOUD or AI in CORE-01. Does not gate any question by itself: the engine's applicableWhen cannot count selections, so the Geography gate uses CTX-05. No score. Never re-weights a score by region (GLOBAL-COVERAGE rule).
scoring.basis: LTM heuristic for the region list: it follows the owner's decisions G1 and G4 and the markets in coverage.ts (eu, uk, ch, us, ca, in, sg, hk, jp, kr, cn, au, nz, gcc, latam, za), grouped so a CIO answers in one breath. EU and UK are separate options because they are separate markets in coverage.ts and their regimes differ since 2020; the owner's note grouped them, and merging is a one-line change.

questions.prompt: Roughly what share of technology operations effort, in-house and contracted, is delivered onshore?
questions.intent: Record the onshore, nearshore and offshore delivery mix as context for the workforce and vendor sections and for data-access and sovereignty routing.
questions.answerDesign: Working definitions, LTM's own: onshore is delivered in the country where the organisation mainly operates; nearshore is another country in the same or an adjacent time zone; offshore is a distant time zone, typically a lower labour-cost location. Count in-house staff and contracted providers together.

options.label: 60% to 90% onshore; the rest nearshore or offshore
30% to 60% onshore; the rest nearshore or offshore
Under 30% onshore; mostly nearshore or offshore

scoring.note: Feeds the workforce and vendor narrative (a blended labour cost differs by location, and Cost IQ does not compare rates), the interpretation of CORE-36 (external workforce share) and ADP-17, 18, 35 and 36 (sourcing), and a routing suggestion to Sovereign IQ when delivery is outside the client's home region and CTX-03 includes EU, UK or CH (remote access to data from another country). Do not read a higher offshore share as better or worse. No score. Never re-weights a score (GLOBAL-COVERAGE rule).
scoring.basis: LTM heuristic. No published definition of onshore, nearshore and offshore with method and sample was sourced in this task; the definitions in the help text are LTM's working definitions and are labelled as such. Bands follow CORE-36's pattern (shares with Unknown).

core03core04Rewrite.needsOwnerReason: Changes what every client sees on two required questions, introduces conversion rates the owner must accept as registered assumptions, and decides whether saved option IDs are kept.
core03core04Rewrite.problem: CORE-03 and CORE-04 offer bands in US dollars only (labels 'Below US$100M' and so on). Neither feeds a score, finding or the report today (VALIDATION section 12).
core03core04Rewrite.recommendation: Yes: rewrite both so the bands are relative to the client's reporting currency (CTX-01). Recommended design (A): keep the seven and six size classes and their option IDs; show labels from bandTables for the chosen currency. Every table is a conversion of the USD edges at one dated ECB reference rate, rounded to two significant figures, and is a registered assumption (assumptions A1 to A3). Never converted at run time and never by a hidden default.

proposedWording.CORE-03: What is the organisation's approximate annual revenue, in your reporting currency? (Bands are shown in the currency you chose. They are size classes, approximately equal to the US dollar bands at the rate stated under Assumptions.)
proposedWording.CORE-04: What is the approximate annual technology spend currently in scope for this assessment, in your reporting currency? (Same size classes as above.)
proposedWording.help: Band labels follow the reporting currency chosen in the previous question. Where the currency is Other, AED or SAR, or no sourced rate is registered, the bands are shown in US dollars and labelled as such; pick the nearest band at your own rate.

core03core04Rewrite.idHandling: Keep the existing option IDs (LT100M, 100M_500M and so on). They name USD size classes and are read by no score. Cost: a raw saved record shows an ID that reads as dollars; record clientCurrency with it. Alternative: rename to neutral IDs (SIZE_1 to SIZE_7) with a one-off mapping of saved answers; cleaner, more work. Owner chooses.
core03core04Rewrite.alternativeB: Alternative (B), not recommended now: replace the bands with a numeric entry in the reporting currency and derive the band only if a USD comparison is ever needed. It removes conversion entirely but needs a numeric input type the page does not have (interaction types today: single-select, multi-select, slider, range rendered as options, stars, ranking).
core03core04Rewrite.conversionRule: Conversion happens in exactly one place: building the band-label table. Cross rate = (currency per EUR) divided by (USD per EUR), from the ECB reference rates dated 2 Nov 2026. Re-issue the table when the owner approves a new date. The report states the date and the source.
core03core04Rewrite.noConversionElsewhere: The engine scores no money, so no conversion is needed for scoring. Percentage levers apply to amounts in the client's currency. Any later figure that mixes currencies (for example Cost IQ plus FinOps IQ in a single total) needs a registered rate of its own.

rateSource.title: ECB euro foreign exchange reference rates: published around 16:00 CET on working days, 29 currencies, 'for information only' and strongly discouraged for transactions. Rates dated 2 Nov 2026 read 3 Nov 2026 from the daily XML through a summarising fetch tool; regenerate from the XML when the tables are built

bandTables.rounding: two significant figures, displayed with 'M' (million), 'bn' (billion) or 'trillion'; Indian crore is a presentation choice for the owner
bandTables.status: INDICATIVE and UNAPPROVED: generated by a script from rates read through a summarising fetch tool. Regenerate from the ECB XML and have the owner approve before the labels are used.
bandTables.notCovered: AED and SAR are not in the ECB list. Both are pegged to the US dollar in practice (AED 3.6725 reported by secondary sources only; the central-bank page was not found; SAR not searched), so no table is proposed until a central-bank source is read. They, and OTHER, fall back to US dollar bands with a visible label.

assumptions.what: Reporting currency band conversion for CORE-03 and CORE-04
assumptions.value: USD band edges converted at ECB euro reference rates dated 2 Nov 2026 (cross rates through EUR), rounded to two significant figures
assumptions.basis: published source: ECB euro foreign exchange reference rates (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/euro_reference_exchange_rates/html/index.en.html), read 3 Nov 2026
assumptions.confidence: medium (the rate is real; a size class does not need precision)
assumptions.ifWrong: A band label is a few percent off its USD size class. No score, finding or lever uses the band, so nothing else moves; labels are re-issued.

assumptions.what: Which currencies get a converted table
assumptions.value: USD, EUR, GBP, CHF, CAD, AUD, JPY, CNY, INR, SGD; AED, SAR and OTHER show US dollar bands with a visible label
assumptions.basis: LTM heuristic: only currencies the ECB publishes a reference rate for
assumptions.ifWrong: A client in an uncovered currency picks the nearest USD band by their own rate.

assumptions.value: 2 Nov 2026; re-issue on owner approval, at least yearly
assumptions.ifWrong: Labels drift from current size classes; the claims register review date forces a refresh.

assumptions.what: Region of published figures in the report
assumptions.value: Stated per source (the Flexera and FinOps Foundation figures are global samples) and compared with CTX-03 in the report
assumptions.ifWrong: A client in a region the sample under-represents reads a global figure as local.
